statement: You are given a directed graph: a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v], each an edge from u to v.
A strongly connected component (SCC) is a largest possible set of vertices in which every vertex can reach every other along directed edges. Every vertex belongs to exactly one SCC.

Find the SCCs with Kosaraju's algorithm: run a DFS to record vertices by finishing time, reverse every edge, then run DFS on the reversed graph in decreasing finishing time; each of those searches collects one SCC. Return the SCCs as lists of vertices, in the order the second pass finds them.

examples.explanation: Vertices 0, 1 and 2 lie on the cycle 0 → 1 → 2 → 0, so they form one SCC. From 3 and 4 there is no way back, so each of them is an SCC on its own.
The edges form one directed cycle through all four vertices, so the whole graph is a single SCC.
